newsitem.title: USA: ABC/Money consumer comfort index down in Nov 3 wk.
newsitem.headline: ABC/Money consumer comfort index down in Nov 3 wk.

text.p: The Money Magazine/ABC News consumer comfort index slipped two points to -9 in the week ended November 3 from the previous week but remained higher than its -14 level of a year earlier.
It was the second straight week-to-week decline for the index, which hit an eight-year high three weeks ago.

The poll of consumer attitudes reflected political affiliations during the runup to the U.S. elections. Most Democrats were "buoyant" while "confidence among traditionally upbeat Republicans continued to erode" and independents' attitudes "sank", Money Magazine said in a press release.
Respondents' confidence in the economy remained unchanged at -16.
Confidence in personal finances fell to 16 from 18, and Americans' rating of buying climate fell two points to -26.
Regionally, confidence fell in the South, Midwest and in the West, while it rose in the Northeast, according to the index.
The 10-year-old index remains substantially higher than its all-time low of -50 in February, 1992. Its general trend has been higher this year after hovering around -20 throughout most of 1995.

The survey, this time with 1,032 respondents, polls consumers nationwide about the national economy, their own finances and their willingness to spend money. The poll has a margin of error of plus/minus 3.5 percent.
